hero.subtitle: A fall at a Culver City store, apartment complex, or office building can leave you with injuries and unanswered questions. Our team handles premises liability claims across Los Angeles County and can review what happened to you.

about.title: Culver City Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Culver City's mix of retail corridors along Washington Boulevard, office campuses, and residential complexes near Sepulveda Boulevard means plenty of foot traffic on floors, stairwells, and parking structures that property owners are responsible for maintaining. When a wet floor, broken step, uneven pavement, or poor lighting causes a fall, California law asks whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. That's often the crux of a premises liability claim. Because surveillance footage at many Culver City businesses gets overwritten within days or weeks, and because memories of a spill or a broken handrail fade fast, early documentation matters. We don't promise any result, but we can evaluate what happened, help preserve evidence, and explain your options under California's two-year filing deadline (shorter if a government entity is involved).

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: Proving Notice Isn't Automatic
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to build that case.

items.title: Video Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Culver City businesses recycle surveillance footage within days. Acting quickly to request preservation can make the difference in showing exactly how and why a fall happened.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you were partly distracted or wearing certain shoes, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover damages reduced by your share of fault, rather than being barred entirely.

items.question: I fell at a store near Washington Boulevard and didn't report it right away. Is it too late?
items.answer: Not necessarily, but time matters because surveillance footage and witness memories fade quickly. California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though that window shrinks if a government-owned property is involved. Speaking with an attorney soon can help preserve what evidence is left.

items.question: What if the property owner says I wasn't paying attention?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your percentage of responsibility rather than eliminated outright. We can help evaluate the specific circumstances, like lighting, warning signs, or hazard visibility, to assess how fault might be allocated.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No, your initial consultation is completely free. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
